questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Can a corporation give directly to a candidate's campaign?
questions.why: Corporations and unions can't contribute to federal candidates. They can form PACs, or give to super PACs.

questions.prompt: A super PAC airs a $1,000 ad on Oct. 20. How fast must it tell the FEC?
questions.why: From Oct. 15 to Nov. 1, independent expenditures of $1,000 or more must be reported within 24 hours.

questions.prompt: How often do House and Senate campaigns file their regular reports in an election year?
questions.why: Candidate committees file quarterly, plus 12 days before and 30 days after each election. Monthly filing is only an option for PACs and parties.

questions.prompt: In CA's 22nd District House race, outside money favors Democrats by $3.3M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Republican leads fundraising by $2.3M.
